title: How to Outwit the Six Ghosts of Fear
coreMove: Fear loses power when you name its pattern, decide before doubt hardens, cut negative influence, and expose the alibi that lets inaction wear a careful face.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders whose money fear blocks outreach
exampleSpecs.stakes: a late client payment is being mistaken for proof that the whole plan is unsafe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show poverty and criticism fears named before a prompt business move

exampleSpecs.audience: committee leads stuck in repeated review cycles
exampleSpecs.stakes: each delay makes the group feel wiser while fear becomes harder to see
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: break the indecision, doubt, fear, and worry chain with a dated choice

exampleSpecs.stakes: routine complaint loops are feeding mental drift before the plan starts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use self-analysis to trace negative influence and alibis

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who confuse group cynicism with judgment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a message thread is making fear feel like common sense
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show negative influence removed before the first work block

exampleSpecs.audience: professionals whose health worry displaces useful action
exampleSpecs.stakes: caution is sliding into hypochondria after normal evidence arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: separate evidence about ill health from worry and hypochondria

exampleSpecs.audience: skilled workers tempted to shrink desire near a deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: old age and death fears are dressing in practical language
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: name the old age and death alibi before choosing a plan
